q: 1. The plain ends of cast iron pipes are joined by
explain: Dresser coupling is a mechanical joint used to connect plain-ended pipes, offering flexibility and ease of assembly.

q: 2. Garbage is a
explain: Garbage refers to decomposable solid/dry waste, specifically organic matter from kitchens and food handling.

q: 3. The water from kitchens, bathrooms, wash basins is called
explain: Sullage is waste water from households that does not contain human excreta (from baths, kitchens, etc.).

q: 4. The quantity of liquid waste which flows in sewers during rainy seasons is called
explain: Storm sewage (or storm water) refers to the runoff generated by rainfall during the rainy season.

q: 5. A sewer which receives storm water, surface run-off and sewage is called a
explain: A combined sewer carries both sanitary sewage (domestic/industrial) and storm water in a single pipe.

q: 6. A sewer which receives sewage from the collection system and conducts it to a point of final disposal is called a
explain: The outfall sewer is the final section of the sewer line that carries the collected sewage to the treatment plant or disposal point.

q: 7. A pipe conveying sewage from the plumbing system of a single building to a common sewer is called
explain: House sewers (or house drains) connect the building's plumbing to the lateral or public sewer.

q: 8. A sewer which receives discharge of a number of houses sewers called a
explain: Lateral sewers collect waste from individual house sewers and discharge them into branch or main sewers.

q: 9. A sewer which gets discharge from two or more main sewers is called
explain: A trunk sewer is a large pipe that receives sewage from multiple main sewers for transport to a treatment plant.

q: 10. The self cleaning velocity, in order to prevent settling down of sewage in a large sewer is
explain: A velocity of approximately 0.75 m/s is required to ensure that solids do not settle at the bottom of the sewer pipes.

q: 11. The water carriage sewage system removes
explain: Water carriage systems use water as the medium to transport domestic, industrial, and often storm water through underground pipes.

q: 12. A combined system will be favourable when
options: the sewers are to be laid in rocks
the topography is flat necessitating deep excavation
the locality to be served had narrow streets
explain: Flat topography makes a combined system more favorable because laying two separate pipes would require twice the deep, expensive excavation.

q: 13. A separate system will be favourable when
options: the sewers are to be laid in rocks
the topography is flat necessitating deep excavation
explain: Separate systems are generally better for hilly terrain or rocky areas where storm water can be easily diverted into natural channels, or when budget for large combined pipes is limited.

q: 14. The sanitation system in which a small portion of storm water enters sanitary sewers is known as
explain: In a partially separate system, sewage and storm water from roofs/pavements go into one pipe, while general street storm water goes into another.

q: 15. The storm sewers are essentially required to
options: avoid creation of unfavourable healthy conditions
improve the general appearance of the city
dispose off the first washings of early showers
explain: Storm sewers prevent flooding, remove dirty 'first wash' water from roads, and help maintain city hygiene during monsoon.

q: 16. According to Fanning's formula, the quantity of storm water (Q) in litres per seconds is given by
explain: Fanning's empirical formula for discharge estimation is $Q = CA^{5/6}$ where A is the area.

q: 17. The internal diameter of the sewer should not be less than
explain: Standard engineering practice (and many codes) dictates a minimum diameter of 150mm (15cm) to prevent frequent clogging.

q: 18. For house drainage and lateral connection, we shall use
explain: Vitrified stone ware (clay) pipes are preferred for domestic drainage due to their resistance to corrosion and cost-effectiveness.

q: 19. Egg-shaped sewers are generally used for
explain: While best for combined systems to maintain velocity during low flow, they can technically be used in any system.

q: 20. The cross-section recommended for separate system of sewerage is
explain: Circular sewers are the most efficient and economical choice for separate systems where flow remains relatively constant.

q: 21. An egg-shaped cross-section of a sewer
options: is economical than circular cross section
is more stable than circular cross section
provides self cleaning velocity in dry weather
explain: The hydraulic radius of the egg shape at low flow levels ensures higher velocity compared to a circular pipe, maintaining self-cleaning conditions during dry weather.

q: 22. For the sewers of diameter less than 600 mm, the type of joint preferred is
explain: Spigot and socket joints are standard for smaller diameter pipes, providing easy alignment and sealing.

q: 23. For the sewers of diameter more than 600 mm, the type of joint preferred is
explain: Collar joints are generally used for large diameter concrete pipes (over 600mm) for structural stability.

q: 24. Manholes are, generally, located
options: at all junctions of main and branch sewers
explain: Manholes are essential maintenance access points required whenever the pipe path, slope, or size changes, and at junctions.

q: 25. For large sewers, the maximum distance between manholes should be
explain: In larger, walkable sewers, manholes can be placed further apart, with 300m being a common maximum limit for cleaning operations.

q: 26. The lower portion of a manhole is known as
explain: The working chamber is the lower section of the manhole where a person can stand to perform inspections or cleaning.

q: 27. The minimum diameter of a manholes cover should be
explain: A 50cm diameter is the standard minimum to allow a worker to pass through comfortably.

q: 28. Manholes on sewer lines are provided for
explain: The primary purpose of a manhole is to provide access for periodic cleaning and removal of blockages.

q: 29. A drop manhole is provided if
options: a sewer drops from a height
a branch sewer discharges into main sewer at a higher level
explain: A drop manhole is specifically used when the vertical difference between the branch sewer and the main sewer is more than 0.6m.

q: 30. The equipment used for checking the levels of the sewer inverts is
explain: Boning rods (along with sight rails) are traditional tools used during excavation to ensure the sewer pipe is laid at the correct gradient.

q: 31. A good trap should
options: provide an adequate water seal at all times
explain: The water seal is the most critical feature of a trap, preventing foul gases from entering the building while allowing waste water to flow.

q: 32. Ventilation of house drainage is required to
options: relive the pressure of foul gases
dilute the foul air in the drain
reduce the obnoxious effect of foul air
explain: Ventilation prevents air pressure buildup that could break water seals and helps keep the drainage system free of foul odors.

q: 33. In one pipe system of plumbing
options: the main pipe is connected directly to the drainage system
all the traps are fully ventilated
explain: In a one-pipe system, a single vertical pipe carries both soil (waste from toilets) and waste (from sinks/baths), requiring extensive ventilation for safety.

q: 34. In one pipe system of plumbing, waste water is carried away from
explain: Waste water (sullage) from all these fixtures is collected into the same main pipe as human waste in this system.

q: 35. A pipe used to carry discharge from sanitary fittings like bathrooms, kitchens etc. is called
explain: Waste pipes carry 'sullage'—water that does not contain human excreta.

q: 36. All anti-siphonage pipe is not required in
explain: A single stack system relies on a larger diameter pipe and carefully designed branches to prevent siphoning without needing a separate vent/anti-siphonage pipe.

q: 37. The underground structure in the form of a circular or rectangular tank for the purposes of admitting sewage into it from the intercepting chamber is called a
explain: A cesspool is a watertight underground tank used for the temporary collection and storage of sewage; it must be emptied periodically.

q: 38. The percentage ratio of the oxygen available in sewage to the oxygen required to satisfy one stage of bio-chemical oxygen demand (B.O.D.) is termed as
explain: Relative stability indicates the ability of an effluent to resist putrefaction, expressed as the ratio of available oxygen to the total oxygen required for BOD.

q: 39. In preliminary treatment of sewage, the operation which takes place, is
options: removal of fine dissolved organic material
removal of harmful bacteria and other organisms
explain: Preliminary treatment involves physical processes like screening and skimming to remove large floating objects and lighter materials like grease or oil.

q: 40. In secondary treatment of sewage, the operation which takes place is
options: removal of heavier suspended inorganic material
removal of fine dissolved organic material
explain: Secondary treatment is biological; it uses microorganisms to decompose and remove dissolved and colloidal organic matter from the sewage.

q: 41. The secondary treatment of sewage is carried out by the use of
explain: Trickling filters (and activated sludge processes) are biological units used in secondary treatment to oxidize organic matter.

q: 42. Grit chambers of a sewage plant are usually changed after
explain: Depending on the accumulation rate, grit is typically cleaned or removed from the chambers every 2 weeks to maintain efficiency.

q: 43. Grit should be removed from sewage before
options: their lifting by means of pump etc.
settling of sewage in sedimentation tank
explain: Grit removal is essential to protect pumps from abrasion, prevent pipe clogging, and ensure that primary sedimentation tanks are not filled with inorganic matter.

q: 44. The sewage is treated by aerobic bacteria action in
explain: Aerobic processes occur in trickling filters, oxidation ponds (upper layers), and even to a degree in secondary settling tanks if oxygen is present.

q: 45. The equipment used for removing paper and rags from sewers is called
explain: A claw is a specialized tool used in sewer maintenance to snag and pull out rags, paper, or fibrous materials causing blockages.

q: 46. The equipment used for cleaning the sewers easily is called
explain: Scrapers are pushed or pulled through sewers to remove accumulated silt and deposits from the pipe walls.

q: 47. When the sewage is to be distributed over a level area surrounded by dykes, the method is called
explain: Flooding involves applying sewage to a leveled area enclosed by small embankments (dykes) to allow it to seep into the soil.

q: 48. The bio-chemical treatment of sewage effluent is a process of
explain: Biological treatment uses bacteria to oxidize organic matter into stable inorganic compounds.

q: 49. The amount of oxygen consumed by sewage from an oxidizing agent like potassium dichromate is
explain: COD measures the oxygen equivalent of the organic matter in a sample that is susceptible to oxidation by a strong chemical oxidant.

q: 50. A minimum amount of D.O. desirable in any water body is
explain: While 4 mg/L is a survival limit, 5 mg/L is generally considered the desirable minimum to support a healthy and diverse aquatic ecosystem.
